extracted.intended_audience: Authors, reviewers and readers using the F1000Research publishing platform (scientists, scholars, clinicians)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for submitting research outputs to F1000Research and participating in its open, post-publication peer review process, including reviewer selection, review expectations, versioning, licensing, indexing and commenting. Applies to articles, posters, slides and other documents on the platform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and author qualification
rubrics_metrics.description: F1000Research publishes articles and other research outputs reporting basic scientific, scholarly, translational and clinical research across the physical and life sciences, engineering, medicine, social sciences and humanities. Each article has at least one author who is a qualified researcher, scholar or clinician actively working in their speciality and who has made a key contribution to the article. Articles must be original (not duplications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All research is suitable irrespective of the perceived level of interest or novelty; confirmatory, negative and null results are welcome. See the full list of article types for specific format guidance. Posters, slides and documents are linked to specific gateways/collections and may differ from traditional scholarly publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepublication checks by editorial team
rubrics_metrics.description: Article submissions undergo a rapid initial check by the in-house editorial team before being published with the status 'Awaiting Peer Review'. The team ensures the article is within scope and adheres to ethical and editorial policies, including data policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editorial team will also check that the article is intelligible and written in good English so it is suitable for peer review and that its content can be fully assessed by invited reviewers and readers. If a submission fails the initial checks it will be returned to the authors to address the issues, and if not resolved satisfactorily the article will not be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open and transparent publishing model (NISO standard summary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review takes place after publication and is open and transparent. F1000Research summarises its peer review process using NISO standard terminology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key NISO components used: Identity transparency (all identities visible); Reviewer interacts with: Editor, other reviewers, authors; Review information published: review reports, submitted manuscript, reviewer identities; Post publication commenting: Open. All reviewer names, affiliations and reports are published alongside the article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer selection criteria (authors suggesting reviewers)
rubrics_metrics.description: When selecting reviewers, authors must apply the following criteria: Scientific expertise, level of experience, and independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scientific expertise: reviewers must have demonstrated expertise in the key topics and/or methods, and must have published at least three articles as a lead author in a relevant topic, with at least one article published in the last five years. Level of experience: reviewers should have reached a relevant qualification (in the life sciences, usually a PhD or MD) and have a formal appointment at a recognised institution. Independence: reviewers must not be working at the same institute as the authors, should not be close collaborators or otherwise personally, financially or professionally associated with them. Reviewers must declare any conflicts of interest on the published report. Authors are asked not to contact peer reviewers directly and may nominate opposed reviewers; the editorial team identifies/invites reviewers and provides support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer role — assessment of scientific soundness
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are generally asked to assess whether the research is scientifically sound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically reviewers should consider: whether the work is discussed appropriately in the context of the current literature; whether suitable methods have been used; whether sufficient information and source data have been provided to allow others to repeat every step of the work; whether the conclusions are supported by the findings. For some article types (e.g., Case Reports or Opinion articles) reviewers are asked to comment on the facts and approaches used, not necessarily whether they agree with the author’s opinion. Reviewers are given guidelines specific to each article type and tips for writing a good peer review report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer assessment statuses and meanings
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to their written report, reviewers select one of three statuses: Approved, Approved with Reservations, or Not Approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approved: No or only minor changes required. For original research this means experimental design, including controls and methods, is adequate; results are presented accurately and conclusions are supported by the data. Approved with Reservations: Paper has academic merit but requires a number of small changes or some more significant revisions. Not Approved: Article is of very poor quality with fundamental flaws that seriously undermine findings and conclusions. The approval status is shown on the article together with the reviewer's name, affiliation and detailed report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and indexing criteria based on review statuses
rubrics_metrics.description: An article will be indexed in external bibliographic databases once it has passed peer review, defined by specific combinations of approval statuses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indexing occurs when an article receives either two 'Approved' statuses, or two 'Approved with Reservations' statuses and one 'Approved' status from independent and invited peer reviewers. Editorials do not undergo external peer review and are labelled NOT PEER REVIEWED. An article may be labelled PEER REVIEW DISCONTINUED if the authors had serious difficulties in securing any reviewers after a long period of time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer report publication and editorial check
rubrics_metrics.description: When a peer review report is submitted it undergoes an editorial check to ensure it meets the peer reviewer Code of Conduct and is then published alongside the reviewers’ full names and affiliations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The peer review report is assigned a DOI and is citable independently of the article. Reviewers may read existing peer review reports and respond via the Comments section; authors are encouraged, but not required, to respond openly using Comments. Reviewers should notify the editorial team if authors contact them directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revisions, versioning and re-review expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to publish revised versions of their article and to add author comments to peer review reports. All versions are publicly available and independently citable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A short summary of revisions is displayed at the start of each new version. The most recent version is displayed by default. If authors revise, all reviewers are invited to provide additional reports on the new version; reviewers who gave 'Approved with Reservations' or 'Not Approved' are especially encouraged to re-review to assess whether improvements achieve a better approval status. Articles remain 'living' and can be updated at any time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data availability and deposition expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: F1000Research is an Open Science platform and asks authors to include detailed descriptions of methods and to provide full and easy access to the source data underlying the results to improve reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Source datasets associated with articles are deposited in repositories that meet certain criteria. Articles must include a 'Data Availability' section outlining where the source data can be found, including permanent identifiers assigned by the repository and a reference with details of how to cite the dataset(s). Data associated with articles (not posters/slides/documents unless stated) are made available, where possible, under CC0 to facilitate reuse and prevent attribution stacking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing requirements for outputs and peer review reports
rubrics_metrics.description: F1000Research articles are usually published under a CC BY license. Peer review reports published with an article are available under CC BY. Data are made available under CC0 where possible. Posters, slides and documents are usually CC BY but other CC licenses may apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copyright of the article remains with the current copyright holder (usually the author or their institution). Specific license versions may change and the copyright/license information for each article is shown beneath the abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commenting policy and conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: F1000Research encourages constructive debate; the comment system can be used for open academic discussion between authors, reviewers and readers. Comments are automatically labelled with your role (author, reviewer, or reader).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should focus on the scholarly content presented in the article. To comment or respond to a report you must login/register and accept Terms and Conditions before posting. To comment on a particular reviewer report use the 'Respond' link; to submit a general comment use 'Add a comment'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posters, slides and documents publication rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Posters and slides can be submitted quickly via the single-page submission system and are published immediately on F1000Research; there are no author fees. Documents undergo a basic screen before publication and are linked to a specific gateway or collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Published posters and slides receive a DOI and become citable after a very basic check by in-house editors; they are not peer reviewed and do not appear in bibliographic databases such as PubMed. Documents are screened to ensure they meet criteria defined by collection advisers who invited them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article peer review status display and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: The peer review status of an article is clearly indicated at all stages: 'AWAITING PEER REVIEW' immediately on publication until the first peer review report is published; then the current approval status is displayed and updated as reports arrive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The status appears in the article title and in the Open Peer Review summary box on both the HTML and PDF. As additional reports are received the approval status is updated. Once indexing criteria are met the article and associated peer review reports are deposited in bibliographic services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation format including version and peer review status
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles and peer review reports are citable independently; F1000Research adapts citation to include article version number and details of peer review status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The citation should include two additional elements in square brackets immediately after the article title: the article version number (e.g., version 1) and details of the peer review status (number of Approved, Approved with Reservations, Not Approved). Example format: Authors. Article title [version number; details of peer review status]. F1000Research Year, Volume: Publication number (doi). Peer review reports have their own DOI and recommended citation format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer conflicts of interest and conduct requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must declare any conflicts of interest on the published report and abide by the peer reviewer Code of Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editorial team checks submitted reviewer reports to ensure they meet the Code of Conduct before publication. Reviewers should avoid performing reviews if they are not independent, are close collaborators, or have personal/financial/professional associations that create conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial and advisory oversight (no Editor-in-Chief decision on acceptance)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no Editor (or Editor-in-Chief) to decide acceptance/rejection or to oversee peer review; an in-house editorial team performs checks and invites reviewers, while an Advisory Board provides strategic input and may occasionally advise on issues or act as invited reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editorial team returns submissions that fail initial checks; Advisory Board members are not responsible for standard editorial decisions but provide oversight and occasional review support.
